A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, renamed from BlockFound to BlockScan. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison; v4 also includes a paper checklist.

before.justification: V1 reports original Ethereum and Solana detection experiments, component ablations, hyperparameter studies, and alternative post-detection results in Tables 1–3 and 6.

after.justification: V4 retains these original experiments and adds fine-tuning, contamination, efficiency, backbone, dataset-similarity, and larger-dataset results.

M1.justification: The adopted tokenizer, RoBERTa masked modeling with RoPE and FlashAttention, and top-s reconstruction-based anomaly ranking remain unchanged between v1 Section 4 and v4 Section 3. The new backbone experiments and revised contrastive approaches concern alternatives rather than replacement of the adopted detector.

E1.justification: Ethereum, Solana, and transaction-level anomaly detection remain the coverage. V4 adds an Ethereum evaluation involving 100 attack transactions across 69 vulnerable contracts, but does not map these contracts to v1's five DeFi applications. Whether this broadens application coverage or merely enlarges the sample is unclear.

E2.justification: The four main baselines remain BlockGPT, Doc2Vec/GMM, GPT-4o, and the length heuristic. V4 adds a GPT-4o-FT comparison in Table 7. Its existing CLS-CL and Average-CL comparisons now describe positive-only SimSiam learning instead of v1's application-based positive/negative pairs, although Table 6 values remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V4 introduces a larger Ethereum evaluation with reduced label cross-checking and contract-specific percentage and absolute ranking thresholds. It also tests inserting half the malicious cases into training and fine-tunes GPT using half-transaction completion. These substantially expand experimental procedures while retaining the principal chronological splits and training configurations.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component and hyperparameter studies, v4 adds FlashAttention time/memory ablations, DeBERTa backbone comparisons, training-contamination robustness tests, and a 5-gram BLEU analysis of transaction duplication. These investigate efficiency, architectural dependence, and data-quality concerns absent from v1.

E5.justification: V4 Section 5.1 newly states that results average three independent runs, reiterated in the checklist. V1 gives no corresponding run-count statement. Neither version supplies error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the disclosure does not establish an increase from a known earlier run count.

E6.justification: The main BlockFound/BlockScan scores remain unchanged, but Table 2 revises baseline precisions: at k=5, GPT-4o changes from 37.5% to 60% and Doc2Vec from 16.67% to 20%. V4 adds substantial results in Tables 7–10 and Figure 2 under new conditions. Table 7 nevertheless retains the older GPT-4o precision values.

T1.justification: V4 Section 4 introduces benign and malicious reconstruction-risk definitions and Theorem 4.1, applying a cited domain-adaptation upper bound involving benign loss, H-delta-H divergence, and minimum joint error. V1 contains no corresponding distributional risk analysis. This is a substantial formal addition, although no complete proof is supplied.

C1.justification: V4 makes theoretical support an explicit contribution in the abstract and claims a first open-source, best-performing transformer detector with a theoretical guarantee in the introduction. V1 presents an empirically supported customized foundation model without that guarantee. The principal Ethereum/Solana superiority claims remain.

C2.justification: V4 adds substantive discussion of vocabulary evolution, periodic retraining, attacks resembling benign behavior, contamination tolerance, and reasons GPT fine-tuning fails. Appendix C interprets address-frequency and duplication evidence. Section 4 also newly interprets a larger malicious-loss upper bound as justification for anomaly separation; v1's discussion instead emphasizes explainability and improved prompting.

D1.justification: V4 adds projection/prediction-head and RBF-KDE details, a stated GPT fine-tuning model version and approximately $950 budget, and GPU-memory measurements. Ethereum training time changes from 1.5 to around 2 hours. The principal architecture descriptions, hyperparameter tables, eight-A100 setup, and main repository link are retained.

R1.justification: V4 replaces the narrower existing-techniques discussion with a taxonomy separating intra-transaction, inter-transaction/network, and chain-level temporal detection. It adds substantial GNN and time-series literature and explains their complementary scope, alongside new domain-adaptation, DeBERTa, and SimSiam references. Several general blockchain and foundation-model references disappear.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially rewritten, the general background section is removed, and related work is reorganized. V4 adds separate theory and limitations sections, restructures the appendices around broader impact, algorithms, datasets, and experiments, and expands the contrastive-method explanation. Renaming and conference author/header edits accompany this broader restructuring.

P2.justification: V4 substantially reformats the title and author block and reflows the existing displays. Figure 1 is retained and relocated, training Tables 4–5 become side by side, and the algorithm is reformatted. Four additional tables and the two-panel tabular Figure 2 substantially expand the visual presentation of evidence.

improvement.justification: The added robustness, efficiency, backbone, and larger-dataset experiments, together with more concrete limitations, strengthen empirical scrutiny. However, Section 4's upper bound does not establish the newly claimed guarantee of higher malicious reconstruction loss, and Table 7 conflicts with Table 2's revised GPT-4o precisions. These material benefits and theoretical/reporting concerns prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
